observation.visible_scene: A close-up of a curved, tapered drinking glass (pilsner/tulip style) sitting on a dark, glossy surface. The glass is filled with a golden-amber carbonated liquid covered by a thin white foam head at the rim. A narrow, clear stream of liquid falls into the glass from the top edge of the frame, partially hidden behind the rim. The background is very dark, with soft reddish-pink reflections and a faint highlight streak on the surface to the left of the glass. Numerous tiny bubbles cling to the inner walls and float within the liquid.
visible_changes: The pouring stream from above remains present and roughly continuous throughout the segment, striking the foam/liquid near the center-top of the glass.
The foam head's surface and edge shape shift subtly from frame to frame (small bulges and ripples), consistent with the ongoing pour disturbing it.
The density and distribution of bubbles inside the liquid change slightly, with some rising and the wall-clinging bubble pattern varying.
The overall liquid level and the glass's position stay essentially constant across the excerpt; no clear large rise or fall is visible.
The reddish reflections on the left surface and the glass's bright base highlight remain stable, indicating little to no camera movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the pour started before this segment or continues after it (the stream is already active at t=0 and still active at the last frame).
The source of the liquid and the identity of the drink.
Any settling or completion of the foam that may occur after the clip ends.
uncertain_details: Exact material of the liquid (beer vs. other carbonated beverage) is not confirmable.
Whether the liquid level rises at all is within the noise of the frames; the apparent change is minimal.
Camera is most likely static, but slight motion cannot be fully ruled out from the dark background.
